title: Reconstruct DDPM
summary: Connect the forward noising process to learned reverse denoising, then implement closed-form sampling and the noise-prediction loss.

parts.title: A fixed forward process
parts.prompt: Why is the noising process chosen in advance instead of learned?
parts.answer: A simple Gaussian schedule gives a tractable closed form for q(x_t|x_0) and a known terminal prior. Learning can focus entirely on reversing corruption.
hints: The endpoint should approach standard Gaussian noise.
Closed-form sampling avoids simulating every prior step.

parts.title: Predict noise, not pixels
parts.prompt: Why can the reverse model be trained to predict the epsilon used to create x_t?
parts.answer: Given x_t and t, epsilon identifies the corruption component and determines an estimate of x_0 or the reverse mean. The resulting simple MSE is a reweighted variational objective.
hints: The time embedding tells the model the noise level.

parts.title: Iterative generation
parts.prompt: Why does sampling require many reverse steps in the original DDPM?
parts.answer: Each learned transition removes only the small amount of noise introduced by one schedule step. Starting from x_T, the chain repeatedly estimates and removes noise until reaching x_0.
hints: Training samples arbitrary t, but generation traverses the chain.
Small steps make Gaussian reverse transitions reasonable.

parts.title: Implement forward noising
parts.prompt: Compute q_sample(x0, noise, alpha_bar_t) in closed form.

parts.title: Implement noise loss
parts.prompt: Compute mean squared error between true and predicted noise.
